html:
Long before the first electrode was lowered into cortex, philosophers were asking

the questions that define computational neuroscience: Where does the mind reside? Is perception a passive reception or an active construction? Could thought be a form of computation? What is the relationship between the model and the modeled? This section traces the long arc of these questions from antiquity to the present day, highlighting the ideas that most directly anticipate—or challenge—the framework of the brain as a world-modeling engine.
